import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/credit_fraud.csv')

# Set a style for the plots
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a figure and a set of subplots
fig = plt.figure(figsize=(14, 10))
gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2) # 2 rows, 2 columns grid

# Subplot 1: Distribution of 'amount' for fraudulent vs. non-fraudulent transactions
ax1 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
sns.kdeplot(data=df, x='amount', hue='is_fraud', fill=True, common_norm=False, ax=ax1, palette='viridis')
ax1.set_title('Distribution of Transaction Amount by Fraud Status')
ax1.set_xlabel('Transaction Amount')
ax1.set_ylabel('Density')
# Custom legend labels
handles, labels = ax1.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax1.legend(handles=handles, labels=['Not Fraud', 'Fraud'], title='Is Fraud')


# Subplot 2: Distribution of 'hour_of_day' for fraudulent vs. non-fraudulent transactions
ax2 = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1])
sns.kdeplot(data=df, x='hour_of_day', hue='is_fraud', fill=True, common_norm=False, ax=ax2, palette='magma')
ax2.set_title('Distribution of Transactions by Hour of Day and Fraud Status')
ax2.set_xlabel('Hour of Day')
ax2.set_ylabel('Density')
# Custom legend labels
handles, labels = ax2.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax2.legend(handles=handles, labels=['Not Fraud', 'Fraud'], title='Is Fraud')


# Subplot 3: Count of 'transaction_type' by 'is_fraud'
ax3 = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, :]) # This subplot spans both columns in the second row
sns.countplot(data=df, x='transaction_type', hue='is_fraud', ax=ax3, palette='rocket')
ax3.set_title('Transaction Type Counts by Fraud Status')
ax3.set_xlabel('Transaction Type')
ax3.set_ylabel('Count')
# Custom legend labels
handles, labels = ax3.get_legend_handles_labels()
ax3.legend(handles=handles, labels=['Not Fraud', 'Fraud'], title='Is Fraud')


# Adjust layout to prevent overlapping titles/labels
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95]) # Adjust rect to make space for suptitle

# Add a main title for the entire figure
fig.suptitle('Credit Card Fraud Analysis: Amount, Time, and Transaction Type', fontsize=16)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
